Definition: {a hand (the open one (indicating power, means, direction, etc.)}
BiblicalUsage: We went into the province of Judea, to the house of the great God, and this work goeth fast on, and prospereth in their hands, and Daniel saw a stone cut out without hands, which smote the image upon his feet.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Aramaic hand carries the same weight as the Hebrew: the work prospers in men's hands, and the stone that breaks the kingdoms is cut without hands, and God is in both the working and the breaking.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
